cases.question: Which button swings the sword?
cases.answer: The A button swings the sword.

cases.question: How much does the Blue Candle cost?
cases.answer: The Blue Candle can be purchased for 60 Rupees from a shop reached by walking through the Overworld route described in the walkthrough.

cases.question: How many Heart Containers do I need to get the White Sword?
cases.answer: You need five Heart Containers to receive the White Sword, according to the Items document. The Overworld Quest 1 walkthrough says the cave gives it only with six heart containers, and the Hyrule 3 documents also state at least 5.

cases.question: Which item can I find in Level-3 of the first quest?
cases.answer: In Level 3 of the first quest, you can find the Raft (chunk zelda1:underworld-quest-1-dungeon-3:001 says going down the stairs from the compass room leads to the Raft). Its objectives also list a Heart Container and the third Triforce piece.

cases.question: How powerful is the Magic Sword?
cases.answer: The Magic Sword has Damage 4, making it the most powerful sword in the game and four times as powerful as the wooden sword.

cases.question: How can I sail across the sea?
cases.answer: The Raft allows Link to cross lakes and oceans, but it can only be used at a Dock.

cases.question: Is there somewhere my hearts get refilled without paying?
cases.answer: Yes. A fairy fills 3 of Link's hearts, and in the fairy ponds the fairy fills all of your heart meters. Flashing hearts also refill Link's life meter by one full heart.

cases.question: How can I win cash by gambling?
cases.answer: Walk into the tree in Hyrule 1 section D-2 to play the Money Making Game, and you can also find the Money Making Game cave by bombing the cliff wall just left of center in Hyrule 2 section A-5.

cases.question: What does the old man in Level-4 of the first quest say?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: What can I buy at D-4 in section 2 of the overworld?
cases.answer: At D-4 in Section 2 (2nd Quest), the shop sells Arrows for 80 rupees, the Magical Shield for 130 rupees, and a set of 4 Bombs for 20 rupees.

cases.question: What happens if I register my name as ZELDA?
cases.answer: Entering your name as "Zelda" when you start the game immediately begins the Second Quest without playing the First Quest. The documents do not explicitly say whether the name is case-sensitive, so it is unclear whether "ZELDA" triggers the same effect.

cases.question: Where can I buy the Blue Candle, and what can it be used for?
subqueries: Where can I buy the Blue Candle in Castlevania NES game
What can the Blue Candle be used for in Castlevania NES game
cases.answer: You can buy the Blue Candle for 60 Rupees in a shop reached by walking one screen west from the spot where you find 30 Rupees, after going from the Fairy Fountain three screens south, two west, and then four screens east and two south. It can throw a flame to light dark dungeon rooms, burn bushes in the overworld, and damage enemies, but it can only be used once per screen. It can also burn trees to reveal secrets.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Level-1 in the first quest and how do I defeat him?
subqueries: Who is the boss of Level 1 in the first quest of the NES game The Legend of Zelda?
How do I defeat the Level 1 boss in the first quest of The Legend of Zelda on NES?
cases.answer: The documents do not clearly identify the Level-1 boss of the first quest. The Aquamentus boss guide is listed under Quest 1 Dungeon 1, which suggests Aquamentus is the boss there, and it says to strike his head six times with the Wooden Sword or three times with the White Sword, timing strikes between his energy orbs, and that the Magical Shield absorbs the orbs. However, the Dungeon 1 label is not explicitly stated as Level-1 in the documents' wording beyond the file path.

cases.question: What do I need to enter Level-4 in the first quest, and which item is inside?
subqueries: What do I need to enter Level 4 in the first quest of The Legend of Zelda NES?
Which item is inside Level 4 in the first quest of The Legend of Zelda NES?
cases.answer:
Most relevant excerpts from the sources (no generated summary):
[1] [Objectives] - Obtain the Ladder. - Defeat the 2 headed Gleeok. - Obtain a Heart Container. - Obtain the fourth Piece of Triforce.
[2] Zelda 1 Wiki Reference Note. The Legend of Zelda is a groundbreaking action-adventure game developed by Shigeru Miyamoto and released in Japan on February 21, 1986, for the Nintendo Famicom Disk System. It was the fourth best-selling Famicom game released in 1986, selling approximately 1,690,000 copies in its lifetime. In America it was released as a cartridge with a battery backed up memory chip…
[3] [Objectives > Prerequisites] - Raft. [Objectives > Advised Preparation] - Use the raft to launch off from the dock at D-4 in section one and collect a Heart Container.

cases.question: How do I beat the dragon boss?
cases.answer: The documents don't name a single 'dragon boss,' so both dragon bosses are covered. Aquamentus (a dragon whose fireballs can only be blocked by the Magical Shield) is vulnerable to the Sword and Arrows and can also be killed by two Bombs. Gleeok (a dragon with two, three or four heads) must have every attached head destroyed, since freed heads can't be defeated; dodge their projectiles and focus on the attached heads.

cases.question: How do I defeat Gleeok?
cases.answer: You must stab each attached Gleeok head until it detaches and flies freely around the room, then destroy every one of the attached heads, since free-flying heads cannot be defeated and must be dodged.

cases.question: How do I use the Hookshot?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: Can I ride a horse in this game?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: In the first quest, which dungeon has the Ladder?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: In the second quest, which dungeon has the Ladder?
cases.answer: The documents do not state which dungeon in the second quest contains the Ladder. Dungeon 6 of Quest 2 lists "Obtain the Ladder" as an objective, which points to the Ladder being found there, and Dungeon 7 requires the Ladder as a prerequisite, so it is not a location for it.

cases.question: How can I attack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword. You can also use the B button to fire a subweapon, such as the Magical Wand, which shoots magical blasts.

cases.question: Which button do i have to press to attack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword, which is the attack action in the controls.

cases.question: How can I atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing the sword. Press the B button to use your subweapon.

cases.question: how do i open the menu
cases.answer: Press the Start button on the NES controller to bring up the sub-screen menu, where Link can look at the map and change subweapon. Press Start again to return from the sub-screen to the normal view.

cases.question: can i blow up walls with bombz?
cases.answer: Yes, bombs can blast holes in weak walls, as stated in the Bomb item description. The walkthroughs also describe bombing walls to reveal hidden passages, such as the north walls in Quest 1 Dungeon 1 and the right wall in Quest 1 Dungeon 7.

cases.question: how do i use my secondary item
cases.answer: Press the B button to use your subweapon. To change which subweapon is assigned to B, open the sub-screen with Start and select the one you want with the D-pad.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press the A button to swing your sword. You can also press B to use your selected subweapon.

cases.question: how can i heal?
cases.answer: Fairy Fountain: the overworld guide says to go back to the Fairy Fountain and heal there. Fairies fill all heart meters in the fairy ponds, and a Fairy enemy drop restores 3 hearts. A Water of Life completely refills Link's life bar, and a medicine woman in Hyrule 7 sells Red Potions or Water of Life.

cases.question: where do i find money?
cases.answer: Several spots in the documents have money: the Money Making Game is in a cave immediately left of the start screen, reached by bombing the rock face (zelda1:cheats:004). In the 2nd Quest, Hyrule 8 D-2 has a tree you can burn to reach the richest Red Moblin, who gives 100 Rupees, and B-2 has a stairwell leading to 10 Rupees (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-8:002). Hyrule 1 B-3 has a secret cave giving 30 Rupees after bombing the north wall (zelda1:overworld-hyrule-1:003).

cases.question: what is the best weapon?
cases.answer: The most powerful sword in the game is the Magic Sword, which deals 4 damage and is four times as powerful as the Wooden Sword. Link must have twelve Heart Containers before he can receive it.

cases.question: how do i open a locked door?
cases.answer: One documented method is a cheat: when you enter the first dungeon, immediately leave and come back, and the locked door will open. Otherwise, keys open locked doors, with each key opening one door, and Link can carry up to nine until he obtains the magic key.

cases.question: what do i do if ig im stuck
cases.answer: Per the General Tips, if you're unsure how to proceed through a dungeon, bomb every wall that does not contain a door, since passageways leading further in are typically found this way. It is also common to find passages to rooms in the "eyes" or unmarked rooms on the dungeon map.

cases.question: how do i defeat the dragon?
cases.answer: The dragon is Gleeok, a multi-headed dragon boss. Link must attack each head, and when a head takes enough damage it detaches and flies around the room; the flying heads cannot be hurt, so dodge their projectiles and keep attacking the attached heads until every head is disconnected.

cases.question: where do i get bombs?
cases.answer: In Quest 1, fight and defeat the Moblins in the nearby area until they drop Bombs that you can collect. The Quest 2 overworld list also includes getting some Bombs, but it does not say where.

cases.question: how do i unlock the bow?
cases.answer: In Quest 1, Dungeon 1, the Bow is found in room O-1, a room with Traps in each corner and a stairwell in the center surrounded by blocks. Push the left most block aside to enter the stairwell, where you'll find the Bow. You'll need to purchase Arrows to use it, unless you already bought them before finding it.

cases.question: how do i save my game?
cases.answer: To save, choose "SAVE" with Select and press Start on the Game Over screen, which stores your accomplishments until you next play. You can also press Up (D-pad) and A simultaneously on the second controller from the sub-screen menu to quickly access the Save Screen.

cases.question: how do i get more hearts?
cases.answer: Heart Containers give an extra heart permanently. You can get them by pushing a tombstone in the Graveyard (Quest 2), burning a tree with the blue candle on Lake Hylia (Quest 1, fourth Heart Container), and using a bomb on a rock near the eastern mountains (Quest 1, sixth Heart Container). Fairies also fill 3 hearts when dropped by enemies.

cases.question: can i buy a better shield?
cases.answer: Yes. A Magical Shield is sold in several places, such as a shop reached by burning a tree in Quest 1 for 90 Rupees, and it reflects more attacks than the Small Shield Link starts with.

cases.question: how do i see in dark rooms?
cases.answer: In dark rooms you can light them with the Blue Candle, as stated in the Dungeon 4 walkthrough. The Blue Candle can light up dark rooms in dungeons but can only be used once per screen. The Red Candle works the same way with no per-screen limit.

cases.question: Which button do I press to jump?
cases.answer: Press the A button to jump in the air; the jump height is fixed and does not depend on how long you hold it.

cases.question: How many spirit points does the windmill star cost?
cases.answer: The windmill star costs 5 spirit points.

cases.question: How many lives does Ryu start with?
cases.answer: Ryu starts the game with two lives in reserve, and he can gain more by finding extra life items.

cases.question: What happens if the clock runs out before I finish a stage?
cases.answer: You lose one life if the timer runs out before you complete a stage.

cases.question: How can I get higher using just one wall?
cases.answer: Use the wall hop technique: jump toward and cling to a wall, hold the jump button, push away from the wall, then immediately push back toward it as you let go. If done correctly, you rise and cling to the wall higher than where you started, and repeating it can take you to the top of the screen.

cases.question: Who attacks me in Stage 2-3?
cases.answer: In Stage 2-3, you are first attacked by the enemy known as Bomberhead as soon as you enter the hall.

cases.question: Who is the boss of Stage 3-3?
cases.answer: The boss of Stage 3-3 (Act III) is Basaquer.

cases.question: What does the fire wheel do and does it use spirit points?
subqueries: What does the Fire Wheel spell do in the NES game?
Does the Fire Wheel spell use spirit points (SP) in the NES game?
cases.answer: The fire wheel surrounds you in fire that eliminates any enemy that contacts you, and it lasts five seconds. It requires no spirit points to use, but it replaces your current secondary weapon.

cases.question: What is Ninja Gaiden called in Europe?
cases.answer: In Europe, Ninja Gaiden is known as Shadow Warriors.

cases.question: how do i atack?
cases.answer: Press B to attack by swinging your sword, and you can attack low by squatting when you attack. Hold Up on the D-pad while pressing B to use your secondary weapon, which requires enough spirit points.

cases.question: how do i get more ninpo?
cases.answer: The documents don't use the term "ninpo," but they describe spirit points, which you must accumulate to use secondary weapons. Blue spirit point tiles give 5 points and red tiles give 10, and Stage 2-1 includes a red Spirit Points tile you can pick up. If you meant spirit points, collect these tiles.

cases.question: how do i heal?
cases.answer: The documents mention health-restoring potions you can collect in several stages: a potion from a lamp at the end of the bridge in Stage 4-2, a health-restoring potion in an insect item in Stage 2-2, a potion in Stage 3-1 over a dock segment, and a health-restoring potion in a candle above the first potion in Stage 5-2. Collecting these items restores health.

cases.question: why did i get sent back to 6-1?
cases.answer: Losing to any of the final bosses sends you back to 6-1, regardless of how many lives you have left. Defeated bosses stay dead, so you will not have to face them again once you return.

cases.question: What is the password to skip to Act 5?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.

cases.question: How do I unlock the second playable character?
cases.answer: There is not enough information in the indexed sources to answer this question.
